title: Internal role reboarding & skill-bridge playbook (90-day)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook standardizes reboarding for employees moving between teams or returning from extended leave (parental, sabbatical, long-term project rotation). It combines a hiring-lite rubric for internal candidates, a targeted skill-refresh plan, and a pragmatic 90-day onboarding checklist to accelerate contribution and reduce cognitive overhead during transitions.

Scope and when to use:
- Internal lateral moves, promotions that require substantial context change, or return-to-role after 8+ weeks away.
- Not intended for full external hire onboarding (use external onboarding playbook).
- Use when the receiving manager expects >2 weeks ramp to independent contributions.

Success metrics (90-day):
- Primary metric: measurable project contribution (merged PR, completed ticket, or feature milestone) within 60 days.
- Secondary: role-competency rubric median >= 3/5 by day 90 (see rubric section).
- Manager confidence score >= 4/5 on handoff checklist by day 90.

High-level timeline (summary):
- Pre-transition (2+ weeks before move) — alignment, access, set expectations.
- Days 0–14 — quiet launch, context soak, shadowing.
- Weeks 3–8 — paired work, ownership of a small deliverable.
- Weeks 9–12 — independent delivery, evaluation, growth calibration.

Pre-transition checklist (HR + receiving manager):
- Confirm start date and public/internal announcement timing.
- Identify a primary buddy and a backup (names + capacity).
- Access matrix: repo permissions, CI, runbooks, slack channels, cloud console roles. Create checklist entries for each and assign owners.
- Training needs: identify 2–3 domain-specific concepts to refresh (e.g., infra patterns, model serving differences, SLOs).
- Kickoff doc: two-page brief (context, success criteria, immediate 30-day goals) created by sending manager.
- If returning from leave: check benefits, equipment status, preferred working cadence.

Day 0 (quiet launch):
- 30m manager welcome: clarity on role, priorities, and first deliverable.
- 60–90m buddy walkthrough of key repos and runbook highlights.
- Calendar block: allocate uninterrupted deep-work windows and daily 30m syncs first week.
- Confirm access and account health (login to 3 critical systems).

Weeks 1–2 (context & low-risk tasks):
- Goal: orient, reduce ambient uncertainty.
- Assign 1 low-risk ticket that touches core codepaths; pair for first iteration.
- Deliver short self-directed doc: "what I learned about X" (one page).
- Micro-eval: manager + buddy complete an initial rubric (baseline).

Weeks 3–8 (ramp & paired ownership):
- Assign a scoped project (2–4 weeks) with clear acceptance criteria.
- Encourage pairing rotations: implement, code review, and deployment handoffs.
- Monthly review: 30/60 goal checkpoint and signal readiness to own on-call or cross-team comms.

Weeks 9–12 (ownership & evaluate):
- Handoff a production-facing responsibility (monitoring, oncall, feature ownership) for a 2-week window with soft rollback support.
- Final 90-day rubric + written go/no-go notes from manager.
- Development plan: 3 concrete focus areas for the next 90 days.

Mentoring and buddying guidance:
- Buddy: 3–4 hours/week for first 4 weeks, 1–2 hours/week for weeks 5–8.
- Expectations doc for buddy: share architecture map, common troubleshooting flows, and top 5 historical incidents.

Internal candidate interview-lite rubric (for competitive internal moves):
- Use for situations where multiple internal applicants apply and an interview is required.
- Format: 45–60m conversational loop + 1 working sample (pairing or take-home <=4hrs).
- Competency buckets (score 1–5, 5 highest):
  * Role fit & impact orientation — understands business context and desired outcomes.
  * Technical adaptability — demonstrates ability to learn adjacent stacks and apply patterns.
  * Collaboration & knowledge transfer — evidence of good handoffs and doc hygiene.
  * Ownership & risk judgment — balanced tradeoffs, incident handling examples.
  * Learning plan realism — practical steps candidate will take to close gaps in 30/60/90.
- Decision guidance: median >= 4 with no score <= 2 recommended for hire without further study.

Evaluation rubric template (short):
- 5: Exemplary; can coach others and independently deliver across unknowns.
- 4: Strong; limited context gaps and requires minor ramping.
- 3: Solid; will need routine pairing for nontrivial tasks.
- 2: Partial; significant gaps that require focused training.
- 1: Not ready; role mismatch or needs long-term remediation.

90-day checklist (manager-facing, binary items + notes):
- [ ] Kickoff brief created and shared.
- [ ] Buddy assigned and schedule agreed.
- [ ] Access matrix completed (list systems + verified).
- [ ] Small deliverable completed and reviewed.
- [ ] Scoped project started and progress visible.
- [ ] Oncall or operational responsibility shadowed.
- [ ] Final rubric completed and archived.
- Notes: 

30/60/90 goal template (to share with employee):
- 30-day: context + one measurable deliverable (e.g., ship small fix, document a service).
- 60-day: own a cross-service flow, reduce mean time-to-restore for assigned alerts by X%.
- 90-day: deliver a project milestone and mentor a peer on one domain-specific task.

Manager playbook for giving feedback:
- Weekly 1:1s first 6 weeks with written 2–3 sentence takeaways stored in the kickoff doc.
- Use concrete evidence (PR links, incident notes) to justify rubric scoring.
- If at day 45 the median rubric < 3, initiate a focused remediation plan (4–8 weeks) or consider role re-scope.

Knowledge capture & closure:
- The transferee must produce a 1-page lessons-learned doc at day 30 and a 2–3 page operating brief at day 90.
- Transfer artifacts (runbooks, infra notes, Slack signals) must be added to the team wiki and linked in the final evaluation.

Optional templates (appendix pointers):
- 1-page kickoff brief (context + 30/60/90 + acceptance criteria).
- Access matrix CSV template (system, owner, verification date).
- Short performance note template for manager (evidence + score + suggested next steps).

Open questions / Known tradeoffs:
- Time budgeting for buddies when multiple reboards are active — recommend rotational buddy pool.
- Measuring success for roles where contribution is nonprofit or long-cycle (use proxies like design artifacts completed).

Quick start cheat-sheet (one-liner checklist for manager):
- Create kickoff brief, assign buddy, verify access, block deep-work, assign 1 small fix, run weekly syncs, record rubrics at day 14/45/90.

Document history and owners:
- Created by: Aisha Patel (People Ops)
- Primary reviewers: Marco Ruiz (Eng Manager), Evelyn Zhang (Head of Internal Mobility)
- Suggested next review: 2025-08-01
notes: This file is intended as a living drive doc; prefer light prose and actionable checklists — move finalized items to Confluence templates later.
